description: Synthetic version of the Kaggle credit card fraud dataset with a 5% fraud rate. Rows 0-284806 are ALL original transactions, unchanged and in the original order. Rows 284807-299278 are synthetic fraudulent transactions.
artificial_data_statement: The synthetic transactions are ARTIFICIAL. They are random numerical variations of real fraudulent rows and are NOT real-world fraud records. V1-V28 are anonymised PCA components, so the variations do not represent any specific real-world fraud technique. Use only for additional experiments and demonstrations; never for the official baseline or Improved v2 evaluation.
target_rule: Keep all original rows; final_fraud = round(0.05 * legitimate / 0.95)
source_selection: Each synthetic row has one source row drawn uniformly at random WITH replacement from the 492 original rows where Class == 1 (numpy default_rng(42).integers).

perturbation_formula.Time: t_new = clip(round(t_source + epsilon * sigma_time * z_t), time_min, time_max)
perturbation_formula.Class: 1 (copied label; never used to compute the variation)
perturbation_formula.z: independent standard normal draws, one per value

perturbation_parameters.random_generator: numpy.random.default_rng(seed); draws in this order: source rows (integers), z for V1..V28 (n x 28), z for Amount (n), z for Time (n)
perturbation_parameters.sigma_source: standard deviation (ddof=1) over the original fraud rows

leakage_warning: Synthetic rows are derived from ALL 492 original fraud rows, including the 98 in the official test set (models/test_indices.csv), and the original legitimate rows include the rows both models were trained on. Do not evaluate the existing models on this file as if it were unseen data.
